title: The burnt helicopter on Núi Bà Đen
description: A man in a dark beret and camouflage fatigues stands squarely in front of the crumpled, partly burned wreckage of a helicopter on a brushy hillside — buckled fuselage panels, a scorched mass at right, torn interior surfaces at left, snapped saplings around it. Larry names him as Trung Xi Nhat Nham, an interpreter who spoke nine languages and who he says was protecting him, and places the wreck on Núi Bà Đen. The wreck, he says, was already there when he got to Vietnam; seven men died in it, and it burned for three hours. He does not know whose helicopter it was.
researchNotes: His words of 2026-09-02 (giscus-vn-0148-c18259776.json), against the standing question "Whose helicopter went down here? Did everyone get out?" — the second half is answered and the first is not. Asked plainly on 2026-09-03 whether he saw it come down, he said: 'It was already there when I got to Vietnam. After the CBC people. After the rocket launch.' (2026-09-03-phone-burnt-helicopter.json, linked to this frame 2026-09-14). So the crash predates his arrival, and 'seven dead' and 'burnt for three hours' are what he was told, not what he saw; the second and third sentences bear on when the photograph was taken, not when the aircraft came down. The photograph's date is left unknown: he gave none, and none is inferred from the roll position. SEARCHED 2026-09-03, NEGATIVE FOR HIS TOUR: a sweep of the VHPA and DIA helicopter loss records for September 1964 to September 1965 found no loss at Núi Bà Đen or anywhere in Tây Ninh province (scope and limits: aircrew named on the Wall only, so non-American or passenger-only losses are invisible). A reading of the wreck itself on 2026-09-09 found the scan too coarse to identify the airframe; no engine type or paint colour is evidence from this file. Research on the pre-arrival window continues in research/events/nui-ba-den-helicopter-wreck.md (ledger #21, issue #89) and is deliberately not summarised here. The man in the frame is a new person record (data/people/trung-xi-nhat-nham.json); a reading of his name that affects how it should be searched is filed in research/ and deliberately not repeated here.
